key_insight: A physics-constrained, multi-fidelity turbulence modeling framework can deliver formal computational cost growth of O(log(Re)) while preserving accuracy across Reynolds-number extrapolation.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical path toward cheaper, scalable CFD predictions for wall-bounded turbulent flows without sacrificing key flow features like separation and near-wall behavior.
method: Start with Spalart–Allmaras RANS as the low-cost baseline.
Use field inversion and machine learning to learn a constrained correction that preserves the law of the wall.
Train at affordable low-Re cases and deploy the model to higher-Re flows under fixed-grid/solver assumptions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful transfer from training at Re_τ=1000 to Re_τ=5200 in channel flow, and from Re_b=5600 to 10595, 19000, and 37000 in periodic hill flow, with the lowest RMS error and nearly Reynolds-number-independent error.
watch_item: The O(log(Re)) cost claim relies on stated assumptions about grid alignment, fixed spanwise resolution, and steady-solver scaling, so performance and cost may change when these conditions are not met.
paper_title: A formal log(Re)-cost framework for the engineering turbulence problem
